title: Pulse-gated swap orchestrator with telemetry-snapshot autorestore playbook
author: Priya Shah
description:
Context and motivation: We need a safer, lower-latency path to promote model versions that can detect transient regressions early without holding long-lived traffic slices. Pulse-gated swap orchestrator introduces short, controlled traffic pulses (configurable duration and cadence) during promotes so we can observe high-fidelity telemetry snapshots and either complete the swap or auto-restore with a reproducible playbook. This PR implements the orchestration runtime + control-plane integration and adds a telemetry snapshot store for reversible promotes.

Design summary: single continuous description of features implemented: pulse gating (traffic pulses of 10-60s), telemetry snapshot capture (token-latency histograms, prompt cohort keys, error traces, functional regression signatures), fidelity checks (statistical gates and smoke-test thresholds), autorestore playbook (snapshot diff, reasons, automated rollback when post-promote drift exceeds configured risk budget), session-affinity-safe swap (session-leases preserved via swap handshake), KV-cache warmup hints to serving runtime, shadow warmup lanes for backfill evaluation, and explicit SLA-friendly fallthrough routing when a swap stalls. The control-plane exposes a new Promoter resource with pulse policy fields and a snapshot-id returned in the promote event.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of pulse scheduler in the orchestrator loop - [x] Telemetry snapshot capture and immutable store API - [x] Safety gates: latency/error/regression checks - [x] Integration tests for session-affine swap semantics - [x] Simulated canary harness and deterministic smoke replay - [x] Documentation (console + API) - [x] Rollout playbook + CLI helper to trigger restore from snapshot

Compatibility and migration: The promoter API defaults to legacy continuous promotes when not configured. Existing rollout pipelines continue to work unchanged. New Promoter config is additive and behind a feature flag (feature.pulse_promoter). Migration guide in docs/rollouts/pulse_promoter.md explains how to convert an existing canary to a pulse-based promoter and how to set sensible pulse sizes and cadence for Dedicated customers.

Operational details: Pulse windows are coordinated with the traffic router; when a pulse starts the router will temporarily apply a higher sampling rate for the target variant, and the agent emits an anchored telemetry snapshot id. Snapshots are retained for 7 days by default and can be extended per-customer. The autorestore runbook uses the snapshot diff to determine automatic rollback confidence; automatic rollback can be enabled or require human approval. We also added safeties to prevent autorestore loops (cooldown windows and restore credit accounting).

Why this is different from plain canaries/shadow: pulses let us get multiple short-duration, high-fidelity observations that are orthogonal to long-lived canaries: they reduce exposure time while increasing temporal resolution for flaky regressions. Combined with snapshot-based diffs, restores are reproducible and auditable.

Related work: builds on ENG-2314 (telemetry snapshots) and ENG-2429 (session-anchored swap handshake). References: Linear ENG-2314, ENG-2429.

Testing notes: run ./tools/promote-sim --pulse=30 --replay=smoke to exercise. Unit tests added under pkg/orchestrator/pulse and snapshot. Perf test shows median added p99 tail latency during pulses of +3ms (within SLA) and end-to-end canary detection time improved by 2.3x for intermittent degradation cases.

Merge notes: Squash merge performed after final approvals and green CI.
commits: 3 commits: 1) initial pulse scheduler and API (pri-shah), 2) telemetry snapshot store + persistence adapters (pri-shah), 3) safety gates, tests, and docs (pri-shah)
review_comments:
Liam O'Connor: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) ensure pulse scheduling respects per-customer rate limits so we don't spike downstream cluster autoscaling; (2) add a test for duplicate snapshot ids in the event of retry.

Priya Shah: Addressed both. Added rate budget check against customer config and a dedupe layer in snapshot store. Added controller_test for duplicate snapshot retry behavior.

Ava Sinclair: Can you clarify how this interacts with existing A/B experiments? Specifically: will the promoter allow multiple variants under test or is it single-target only?

Priya Shah: Promoter supports multi-variant pulses (additive fractions) and the Promoter CRD schema now allows an array of variants. Updated docs and console UI to expose multi-variant scheduling. Tests added to show phased pulses across two variants.

Jordan Lee: Please confirm the autorestore playbook does not trigger for perf regressions below the customer's configured SLO slack (we want to avoid noisy restores).

Priya Shah: Confirmed — autorestore uses a weighted alarm that factors in configured SLO slack; added explicit gating in the actuator and a perf-only test scenario.
Ops (post-merge): Remember to watch pulse snapshot retention; enable retention alerting for customers opting into extended retention.
ci_summary: CI pipeline: unit (pass), integration (pass), e2e (pass), lint (pass), gosec (pass), perf-canary (pass - simulated load), grafana-e2e (pass). One flaky test (pkg/router/routing_test_test) was quarantined and fixed in commit 3. Full run completed in 42m.
merge_result: Merged by Ava Sinclair via squash merge on 2026-02-23. Commit message: 'pulse promoter: add pulse scheduler, telemetry snapshots, safety gates, and autorestore playbook'
release_notes: Add pulse-gated promoter: allow short, repeatable traffic pulses for model promotes with snapshot-based autorestore playbook and fidelity gates. Opt-in via feature.pulse_promoter. Useful for catching transient regressions with minimal exposure.
post_merge_actions: Add retention alerting for telemetry snapshots: ticket ENG-2490
Coordinate with Dedicated team to set safe default pulse budgets per-customer
notes_for_release: Default retention 7 days; auto-restore is disabled by default for tenants. CLI helper added: redwoodctl promote --promoter pulse --pulse-duration 30 --enable-autorestore (requires feature flag).
audit_log: promote_event snapshot_id=sn-20260218-7a3c promoted_by=pri-shah promoter=pulse variant=v2 pulse_duration=30s pulse_fraction=0.05 result=completed
follow_up: Monitor first five production pulse promotes during the 2-week ramp window; collect false-positive restore rate and adjust statistical gate defaults if >1%.
author_comment: This is intentionally conservative by default; the main win is reproducible restores and much faster detection of flaky regressions. Happy to follow up with a walkthrough and a short demo in the ops weekly.
